A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CodeDance. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original CodeDance benchmark results, reward ablations, scaling experiments, training dynamics and qualitative reasoning examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports additional execution-success comparisons in Table 3 and a reasoning-depth analysis in Appendix 8.3 and Figure 11.

M1.justification: The executable-code reasoning loop, SFT followed by GRPO, and RBAT sequence-level and turn-level rewards are retained. Renaming the cumulative return in Equation 2 and reiterating previously disclosed hyperparameters do not change the method.

E1.justification: v2 Figure 11 adds evaluated AIME23–25 examples alongside retained benchmarks; this task set is absent from v1. The original training sources and benchmark coverage remain. The added set's sample composition and input format are not described.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds RBAT without turn-level reward to its benchmark comparison. v1 already examined this variant through training curves in Figure 5, but it was absent from Table 3. The external baseline sets in Tables 1 and 2 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 3 adds execution-success rate to accuracy and average turns. The new Appendix 8.3 analysis compares reasoning turns against GPT-4o accuracy as a task-difficulty proxy. These extend the evaluation protocol; the shared model and training/inference settings otherwise remain as stated.

E4.justification: v2 extends the turn-reward ablation with benchmark-level accuracy, turns and execution-success measurements, and adds the difficulty-versus-reasoning-depth analysis in Figure 11. Existing scaling, hyperparameter-sensitivity, training-dynamics and failure-case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces different repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures. The added execution-success rate and mean-turn results are evaluation measurements, not new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 are unchanged, but Table 3 replaces RL results: full RBAT's average accuracy changes from 65.8 to 68.1, and the DeepEyes-reward row from 63.6 to 65.6. New entries include execution success of 0.99 for full RBAT versus 0.91 without turn reward, plus Figure 11 results. Removal of the earlier 150-step disclosure prevents treating the replacements as verified same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The trajectory definition, reward equations, GRPO objective and Appendix 8.2 derivations of reward bounds and the sign-transition threshold are retained. Equation 2 changes return notation without changing its mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and concluding discussion retain the same principal claims: executable visual reasoning, adaptive tool rewards, emergent composition and transfer, and competitive benchmark performance. The new analyses support these existing claims rather than redefine the contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 now explicitly links removing turn-level reward to poorer execution reliability. Appendix 8.3 interprets longer reasoning on tasks with lower GPT-4o accuracy as evidence of difficulty-adaptive depth. Existing failure explanations and limitations concerning synthetic data, modality extension and model scale remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes Table 3's explicit statement that each model was trained for 150 steps. Figure 1 also loses the clarification that its DeepEyes example denotes a model optimized using the DeepEyes reward. Sandbox details, prompt templates, Table 4 settings and the project URL are retained; the hyperparameters repeated in Section 3.1 were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: The same 58 cited works and substantive Related Works discussion are retained. The established positioning against fixed-schema tool pipelines and nonadaptive reasoning remains; the Introduction's revised underuse/overuse wording restates the existing motivation.

P1.justification: v2 copyedits the abstract, introduction, methodology and discussion, renames Section 3.2 from Dataset Curation to Data Engineering, and adds acknowledgements and the short Appendix 8.3 subsection. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 is restructured with reordered benchmarks, an additional row and success column, and revised highlighting. v2 adds Figure 11 and adjusts Figure 4's labels and styling. Several appendix tables and figures move, with subsequent figures renumbered; the existing qualitative displays are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens validation of the reward design: beyond v1's training curves, Table 3 directly contrasts execution success with and without turn reward, while Appendix 8.3 adds evidence concerning adaptive reasoning depth. These additions improve support for existing claims without changing the headline results. The benefit is limited by the removed 150-step ablation disclosure and sparse protocol details for the new reasoning-depth analysis.
